picture.summary: A simple one-page site with a dark top bar, a big coral welcome banner, a row of three matching picture cards on a cream background, and a dark footer.

sections.name: a top bar
sections.description: A dark brown strip with the bold site name 'My Site' on the left and four white menu links (Home, About, Work, Contact) toward the right.

sections.name: a big banner
sections.description: A wide coral-orange block with a large bold white title 'Big Title Here' centered and a smaller white line of text beneath it.

sections.name: 3 cards
sections.description: Three white cards with rounded corners and thin gray borders sitting side by side on a cream background, each with a peach picture placeholder, a bold dark title, and two gray placeholder text lines.

sections.name: a footer
sections.description: A dark brown strip at the bottom with centered white text reading 'Footer · made by me'.

title: A warm one-page website
summary: You'll build a simple one-page site with a dark top bar and menu, a big coral banner, three matching picture cards on a cream background, and a dark footer.
outcome: A finished, friendly-looking home page that opens in any browser straight from your project folder.
learns: Placing items side by side with flex
Menu links that jump down the page

simpler.title: Just the heart of the page
simpler.why: A top bar, a banner, one card and a footer give you a real, styled page in about 40 minutes — you can add the rest later!

chapters.title: Colour the top bar and banner

steps.title: Start the page
steps.instruction: Create a file called index.html. Type the first line <!DOCTYPE html>. Under it, open <html> and close it with </html>. Inside, add a <head> part and a <body> part, each with its own closing tag.
steps.why: Every web page needs this frame. The head holds behind-the-scenes info and the body holds what people see.

hints: A page is like a box with two rooms: one for hidden info and one for what you see.
First line: <!DOCTYPE html>. Then <html> ... </html>. Inside it: <head></head> and then <body></body>, each tag on its own line.

concept.title: The page frame
concept.explain: A web page is wrapped in html tags, with a head for hidden info and a body for what you see.
concept.imageQuery: html page structure head body diagram

steps.title: Fill in the head
steps.instruction: Inside the head, add three lines: a <meta> tag with charset="utf-8" so letters show correctly, a <title> that says My Site, and a <link> tag with rel="stylesheet" and href="style.css" to connect your style file later.
steps.why: The title shows on the browser tab, and the link will bring in your colours later.

I can't see the line that connects your style file yet.
checks.name: href

hints: The head needs three small lines: one about letters, one for the tab name, one to connect a style file.
Between <head> and </head>: <meta charset="utf-8">, then <title>My Site</title>, then <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">.

<meta charset="…">
<title>…</title>
<link rel="…" href="…">

concept.title: Page info
concept.explain: The head holds info for the browser, like the tab name and which style file to use.

steps.title: Add the top bar
steps.instruction: Inside the body, add a <header> (the top bar of your page). Inside it put an <h1>, the biggest heading, that says My Site.
steps.why: Now your page has a name at the very top.

checks.say: I can't see your big heading in a top bar yet.

concept.title: Headers and headings
concept.explain: A header is the top strip of a page, and h1 is the biggest, most important heading.

steps.title: Add the menu
steps.instruction: Under your h1, still inside the header, add a <nav> (a menu). Inside it add four <a> links: Home going to index.html, About going to #about, Work going to #work, and Contact going to #contact.
steps.why: A menu lets visitors jump around your page.

concept.title: Links and menus
concept.explain: An a tag makes clickable text, and href says where the click takes you; nav groups the menu links.

concept.title: Footers
concept.explain: A footer is the strip at the bottom of a page, often with contact info or the maker's name.

steps.title: See your page
steps.instruction: Open index.html in your web browser (double-click it). You'll see all your words, but plain and black on white. Next we'll add colour!
steps.why: Seeing your work helps you notice what's there and what's missing.
hints: Find index.html in your folder.
Double-click it, or drag it into a browser window.
If it opens in a text editor, right-click and choose Open With, then your browser.

quiz.question: Which tag makes a clickable link?
quiz.explain: The a tag makes a link, and href says where it goes.

steps.title: Style the whole page
steps.instruction: Make a new file called style.css. Write a rule for body with margin: 0; (removes the gap around the page edge), font-family: Arial, sans-serif; (the letter style) and background: #f9f6f1; (a cream colour).
steps.why: Your whole page gets a warm cream background and cleaner letters.

checks.say: Your page background isn't cream yet.
There's still a gap around the edge of your page.
Something in your style file looks unfinished. Check your curly brackets and semicolons.

hints: A style rule names a part of the page, then lists how it should look inside curly brackets.
Write body { } and inside put margin with 0, font-family with Arial, sans-serif, and background with #f9f6f1. End each line with a semicolon.

concept.title: Style rules
concept.explain: A style rule picks a part of the page and lists how it should look, like its colour or spacing.

steps.title: Colour the top bar
steps.instruction: Under the body rule (leave a blank line), add a rule for header with background: #3d3030; (dark brown), color: #ffffff; (white text) and padding: 10px 30px; (padding is the space inside the box).
steps.why: Your top bar becomes a dark strip with white writing.

checks.say: Your top bar isn't dark yet.
The writing in your top bar should be white.
Your top bar needs some space inside its edges.

hints: Give the top bar a dark colour, white text and some breathing room.
Write header { } with background #3d3030, color #ffffff and padding 10px 30px.

concept.title: Colour and padding
concept.explain: color changes the text colour, and padding is the space between the edge of a box and what's inside.

steps.title: Put the title and menu side by side
steps.instruction: At the top of the header rule, right after header {, add display: flex; (lines things up in a row), justify-content: space-between; (pushes them to opposite ends) and align-items: center; (centres them up and down).
steps.why: Your site name sits on the left and the menu on the right, on one line.

checks.say: Your title and menu aren't in one row yet.
The menu should be pushed to the right side.
Your title and menu should be lined up in the middle.

hints: Three lines will put things in a row, spread them apart and line them up.
Right after header {, add display: flex, justify-content: space-between and align-items: center.

concept.title: Flexbox
concept.explain: display: flex puts the things inside a box in a row, and other lines decide how they spread out.

steps.title: Style the menu links
steps.instruction: Under the header rule, add a rule for nav a with color: #ffffff;, margin-left: 20px; (space on the left of each link) and text-decoration: none; (removes the underline).
steps.why: Your menu links turn white, spaced out, without underlines.

checks.say: Your menu links still have space missing between them.
Your menu links should be white.
Your menu links still have underlines.
checks.question: Does the nav a rule set text-decoration to none?

hints: Make the links white, add space between them, and remove the underline.
Write nav a { } with color #ffffff, margin-left 20px and text-decoration none.

concept.title: Spacing and underlines
concept.explain: margin is space outside a box, and text-decoration: none takes away the line under links.

steps.title: Make links glow on hover
steps.instruction: Under the nav a rule, add a rule for nav a:hover with color: #f2c6a5; (a peach colour). :hover means 'when the mouse is over it'.
steps.why: Links change colour when you point at them, so people know they can click.

checks.say: Your links don't change colour when the mouse is over them yet.
checks.question: Does style.css have a nav a:hover rule that sets color to #f2c6a5?

checks.say: Something in your style file looks unfinished. Check your curly brackets.

hints: You can give links a different colour just for when the mouse is on top.
Write nav a:hover { } with color #f2c6a5 inside.

concept.title: Hover
concept.explain: :hover gives something a different look only while the mouse pointer is on it.

steps.title: Colour the banner
steps.instruction: Under the hover rule, add a rule for .banner (the dot means 'the thing with class banner') with background: #e07b60; (coral), color: #ffffff;, text-align: center; (centres the text) and padding: 60px 20px;.
steps.why: Your welcome area turns into a big, bright coral banner.

checks.say: Your banner isn't coral yet.
The banner text should be in the middle.
Your banner needs more room above and below the text.

hints: Give the banner a coral colour, white centred text and lots of space.
Write .banner { } with background #e07b60, color #ffffff, text-align center and padding 60px 20px.

concept.title: Centring text
concept.explain: text-align: center puts lines of text in the middle of their box.

steps.title: Make the banner title huge
steps.instruction: Under the .banner rule, add a rule for .banner h2 with font-size: 44px; (how big the letters are) and margin: 0;.
steps.why: Your banner title becomes big and bold.

checks.say: Your banner title isn't bigger yet.
Your banner title still has extra space around it.

hints: Make the letters of the banner title much bigger.
Write .banner h2 { } with font-size 44px and margin 0.

concept.title: Text size
concept.explain: font-size sets how big the letters are, often in px (tiny dots on the screen).

quiz.question: What does padding do?
options: Adds space inside a box, around its content
quiz.explain: Padding is the space between a box's edge and what's inside it.

steps.title: Put the cards in a row
steps.instruction: Under the .banner h2 rule, add a rule for .cards with display: flex;, gap: 20px; (the space between the cards) and padding: 40px 30px;.
steps.why: Your three cards line up side by side with space between.

checks.say: Your cards aren't side by side yet.
Your cards need some space between them.

hints: Use the same row trick as the top bar, plus space between cards.
Write .cards { } with display flex, gap 20px and padding 40px 30px.

concept.title: Gap
concept.explain: gap adds equal space between the things lined up in a row.

steps.title: Make each card a white box
steps.instruction: Under the .cards rule, add a rule for .card with flex: 1; (each card takes an equal share of the row) and background: #ffffff;.
steps.why: All three cards become the same width and white.

checks.say: Your cards aren't sharing the row equally yet.
Your cards should be white.

hints: Make the cards equal width and white.
Write .card { } with flex 1 and background #ffffff.

concept.title: Equal shares
concept.explain: flex: 1 tells each box in a row to grow and take the same share of space.

steps.title: Round the cards
steps.instruction: Inside the .card rule, under the background line, add border: 1px solid #d9d4cd; (a thin line around the card), border-radius: 12px; (rounds the corners), padding: 15px; and color: gray;.
steps.why: Your cards get soft rounded edges, a thin outline and grey text.

checks.say: Your cards' corners aren't rounded yet.
Your cards need a thin line around them.
The text in your cards should be grey.

hints: Add an outline, round the corners, add inside space and make the text grey.
Under background in .card, add border 1px solid #d9d4cd, border-radius 12px, padding 15px, color gray.

concept.title: Borders and round corners
concept.explain: border draws a line around a box, and border-radius rounds its corners.

steps.title: Darken the card titles
steps.instruction: Under the .card rule, add a rule for .card h3 with color: #3d3030;.
steps.why: Card titles stand out in dark brown above the grey text.

checks.say: Your card titles aren't dark brown yet.

hints: Give just the card titles a darker colour.
Write .card h3 { } with color #3d3030.

steps.title: Fill the picture boxes
steps.instruction: Under the .card h3 rule, add a rule for .picture with background: #f2c6a5;, height: 120px; (how tall the box is) and border-radius: 8px;.
steps.why: Each card gets a soft peach picture area at the top.

checks.say: Your picture boxes are still empty and flat.
Your picture boxes should be peach.

hints: The picture box is empty, so give it a colour and a height so you can see it.
Write .picture { } with background #f2c6a5, height 120px and border-radius 8px.

concept.title: Height
concept.explain: height sets how tall a box is, so even an empty box can show up.

steps.title: Style the footer
steps.instruction: Under the .picture rule, add a rule for footer with background: #3d3030;, color: #ffffff;, text-align: center; and padding: 15px;.
steps.why: The footer matches the top bar and finishes the page.

checks.say: Your bottom strip isn't dark yet.
The bottom strip's text should be centred.

hints: Make the footer look like the top bar, with centred text.
Write footer { } with background #3d3030, color #ffffff, text-align center and padding 15px.

quiz.question: What does border-radius do?
options: Rounds the corners of a box
quiz.explain: border-radius curves the corners of a box.

steps.title: Admire your site
steps.instruction: Refresh index.html in your browser. You should see a dark top bar with a menu, a coral banner, three rounded cards on cream, and a dark footer. Point at a menu link to see it change colour!
steps.why: You built a whole website from an empty folder.
hints: Go back to the browser tab showing your page.
Press the refresh button or F5.
If nothing changes, check that style.css is in the same folder as index.html.
